audit.why: Favoured 4/10 fits 60.2% over 392 games. Verdict kept; the prose under it was written against a version of Aurelion Sol that no longer exists and was rebuilt on the current kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content layer describes the pre-rework Aurelion Sol throughout: 'his star orbit', 'stacked stars', an ultimate that 'repositions you' and 'sets up global picks'. None of that is in the kit.
audit.why: Current kit: Cosmic Creator banks Stardust which permanently improves his abilities; R is Falling Star, a 1250-range stun on 120/110/100 that upgrades into The Skies Descend. There is no orbit, no knockback ult, nothing global.
audit.corrected: Level 6 = a 120s 1250-range stun that also banks Stardust. Late = permanent Stardust scaling on every ability.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions absent: Breath of Light and Astral Flight are both channels your stun cancels; Singularity executes below a health threshold and deals percent-health damage; Astral Flight flies over terrain for 1500 and is his only escape.
audit.why: enemyKit Q and W both carry the channel flag ('interruptible — any CC cancels it'); E carries execute and percentHealth flags; W range 1500 with the terrain flag. ownerKit E is hard CC. All three are named in missingInteractions.
audit.corrected: Hold Flawless Duet for the channel, not the gap; leave a Singularity by the edge, never through the centre; and treat 22s Astral Flight as the all-in clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (lint), the packet reports zero sequencing advice anywhere, and dosFull[2].d called Astral Flight a 'fifteen-second' cooldown.
audit.why: Astral Flight is 22/20.5/19/17.5/16 — 22s at rank 1. Breath of Light 3s, Singularity 12s, Falling Star 120/110/100.
audit.corrected: Real numbers in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and content mid/early.

audit.whatIsWrong: content 'early' says he 'has no true escape'.
audit.why: Astral Flight is a 1500-range flight over terrain — it is exactly a true escape, just one on a 22s cooldown.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to name the 22s window instead of denying the escape exists.

edits.before: He needs minions to hide behind and you eat minions for movement — dance the wave into his face and stun the apology.
edits.after: Breath of Light and Astral Flight are both channels — Flawless Duet cancels either, so hold E for the cast, not the gap.

edits.before: Make the wave a runway and the mage a destination. Astral Flight is the clock this lane runs on — read it before every step forward.
edits.after: Make the wave a runway and the mage a destination. Astral Flight is 22s at rank 1 — step forward on its downtime, never into it.

edits.before: Aurelion Sol wins by landing Astral Flight, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Aurelion Sol wins by stacking Stardust off free farm, pulling you into Singularity's execute, and flying out at 1500.

edits.before: - Aurelion Sol Astral Flight: matchup-defining — His reposition and escape — he is a stationary battery while it is down. Check it before every step-up. - W Defiant Dance is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Astral Flight: 22s at rank 1, flies over terrain for 1500 — he is stationary while it is down. - Breath of Light: 3s channel; your E cancels it. - Singularity: 12s, and its centre executes below a health threshold. - Falling Star: 120/110/100.

edits.after: W joins, but it cuts physical damage only — step out of his Breath of Light instead.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Aurelion Sol's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Four stacks is your damage — build them on the wave, then open on him while Breath of Light is still channelling into the minions.

edits.before: Aurelion Sol burns Astral Flight on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Aurelion Sol burns Astral Flight on nothing — that is a 22-second invitation.

edits.before: Your dashes live in the wave's health bar — shoving mindlessly is deleting your own mobility.
edits.after: Breath of Light is a 3s channel that grows with Stardust — every second you stand in it feeds him.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Every low minion is a dash; shove them away and Singularity's pull has you standing still inside the execute.

edits.after: Level 6: Falling Star is a 1250-range stun on 120s, and it banks Stardust too.

edits.before: Dash onto minions closes the gap before his stars orbit wide enough to poke safely.

edits.before: His R can suddenly reposition you or set up a global pick; respect it after 6.

edits.before: He becomes a lane-dominant scaling threat if left to freely stack stars uncontested.

edits.before: Use minion dashes to skip past his star orbit and get in his face. He's immobile and squishy without stacked stars. Punish any overextension hard since he has no true escape. Deny farm to slow his stacking snowball.
edits.after: Use minion dashes to close while Breath of Light is channelling — your stun cancels it outright. Astral Flight is his only escape at 22s, so punish every step-up while it is down. Deny farm to slow his Stardust.

edits.before: Keep closing gaps before he fully stacks his passive damage. Watch for his ultimate repositioning you into danger or peeling him to safety. Group dives punish his lack of mobility. Don't let him freeze and poke freely from range.
edits.after: Keep closing gaps before Stardust stacks up. Falling Star stuns at 1250 range, so spread before he ults and dive after. Group dives punish a 22s Astral Flight. Don't let him freeze and poke freely from range.

edits.before: If he's allowed to scale, his stacked stars and R make him a global threat. Close him down early in fights before his burst combo lands. Focus dive him the moment fights start since he melts fast. Don't give him free space to stack passively.
edits.after: If he's allowed to scale, Stardust makes every ability of his hit harder. Close him down early in fights before Singularity pulls you in. Focus dive him the moment fights start since he melts fast. Don't give him free space to stack passively.

notes: CHART: rows 0-5 already agree across layers (Irelia). Row 6 did not — content win[6] and the packet levelChart both said 'Aurelion Sol' while full phases[6].side said 'Skill', and phases[6].why described Irelia winning the stage. I moved phases[6].side to 'Aurelion Sol' and rewrote phases[6].why in the same proposal; no paired win[6] edit is possible because win[6] is ALREADY 'Aurelion Sol' — this edit removes a cross-layer disagreement rather than creating one. phases[6].rating was left at 6/10 (it does not contradict either layer). Biggest finding: the entire content layer was written for the pre-rework Aurelion Sol — 'star orbit', 'stacked stars', a repositioning/global ultimate. None of that exists in the current kit and all of it was replaced with Stardust, Breath of Light, Singularity and Falling Star.
